SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY BEFORE YOU START Menopause Is Natural. You Don’t Have to Navigate It Alone. Menopause is a normal stage of life, but the transition can bring changes that affect sleep, comfort, sexual health, and everyday well-being. For some women, symptoms are mild. For others, they can disrupt work, relationships, and quality of life. Effective treatment options are available, including hormone therapy for appropriate patients. But not every woman needs hormone therapy, and not every symptom experienced during midlife is caused by menopause. This guide explains what happens during perimenopause and menopause, how hormone therapy works, available treatments, and what to look for in quality care. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps connects women with licensed healthcare providers who evaluate symptoms, medical history, and individual treatment needs before recommending care. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT Menopause is a natural transition. Suffering through disruptive symptoms doesn’t have to be inevitable. 01

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY KNOW THE STAGES Perimenopause, Menopause & Postmenopause: What’s the Difference? PERIMENOPAUSE The years leading up to menopause, when hormone levels fluctuate and menstrual cycles may become irregular. Symptoms can begin while periods continue. MENOPAUSE The point reached after 12 consecutive months without a menstrual period, when no other cause explains the absence of periods. Natural menopause typically occurs between ages 45 and 55. POSTMENOPAUSE The years following menopause. Some symptoms improve; vaginal and urinary symptoms may persist or develop later. The timing and experience vary. Certain surgeries or medical treatments can change the course of menopause. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Your symptoms, menstrual history, age, and medical background help your provider recommend next steps. SMART PATIENT QUESTION Which stage of the menopause transition am I experiencing, and how might that affect my treatment options? 02

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY RECOGNIZING THE SYMPTOMS Could Hormonal Changes Be Affecting How You Feel? As estrogen levels fluctuate and eventually decline, women may experience: Symptoms may begin during perimenopause, continue after menopause, or change over time. Some are strongly associated with menopause; others have multiple possible causes. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Your provider considers your complete health picture rather than assuming every symptom is caused by menopause. Hot flashes and night sweats Difficulty sleeping Mood changes or irritability Difficulty concentrating or brain fog Vaginal dryness and irritation Discomfort or pain during intercourse Changes in sexual desire Irregular menstrual cycles during perimenopause Urinary urgency or recurrent urinary symptoms SMART PATIENT INSIGHT Your symptoms deserve attention, but the right treatment starts with understanding what may be causing them. 03

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY UNDERSTANDING YOUR HORMONES What’s Happening to Your Hormones? ESTROGEN Plays a role in reproductive health, temperature regulation, vaginal and urinary tissue health, and bone maintenance. During perimenopause, levels can rise and fall unpredictably; after menopause they generally remain lower. PROGESTERONE Helps regulate the menstrual cycle and supports the uterine lining during reproductive years. As ovulation becomes less regular during perimenopause, progesterone production may become irregular. Hormone changes help explain why symptoms vary, but sleep, medications, stress, age, and medical history can also influence how a woman feels. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Treatment decisions are based on clinical evaluation, not simply achieving a particular hormone number. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT A single hormone measurement rarely tells the complete story of the menopause transition. 04

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY TESTING AND DIAGNOSIS Do You Need Hormone Testing to Diagnose Menopause? Not necessarily. For most otherwise healthy women age 45 or older with typical symptoms and menstrual changes, perimenopause and menopause can usually be identified through history and symptoms without routine hormone blood testing. Estrogen and follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) fluctuate substantially during perimenopause, so one test may be misleading. Testing can be useful if symptoms suggest another condition, or when age, menstrual history, or clinical circumstances require further evaluation. A provider may assess thyroid disease, anemia, or other possible causes. Possible menopause before age 40 warrants evaluation for premature ovarian insufficiency. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps offers laboratory testing access at a nearby lab or, when appropriate, with an at-home kit. Providers review relevant results in context. Lab fees are billed separately. SMART PATIENT QUESTION Which tests are useful for me, and what decisions will the results help my provider make? 05

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY UNDERSTAND THE TREATMENT What Is Menopausal Hormone Therapy? Menopausal hormone therapy uses estrogen, sometimes together with a progestogen, to treat certain menopause symptoms. SYSTEMIC HORMONE THERAPY Delivers estrogen throughout the body, including through transdermal patches. It is among the most effective treatments for bothersome hot flashes and night sweats and may help prevent bone loss in selected patients. LOCAL VAGINAL ESTROGEN Delivers estrogen primarily to vaginal tissues to address dryness, irritation, and painful intercourse. PROGESTERONE May be prescribed with systemic estrogen to protect the uterine lining in women who have a uterus. Not every woman needs the same medications or combination. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH A licensed provider determines the appropriate medication, combination, and formulation. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT Hormone therapy isn’t one treatment. Different formulations address different needs. 06

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY SET REALISTIC EXPECTATIONS What Can Hormone Therapy—and Can’t It—Do? SYSTEMIC THERAPY MAY HELP LOCAL VAGINAL ESTROGEN MAY HELP HORMONE THERAPY DOES NOT GUARANTEE Weight loss • Improved memory or concentration • Increased sexual desire • Prevention of aging, heart disease, or dementia Individual responses vary; some patients need adjustments or alternative treatment. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Treatment goals should be realistic, personalized, and reviewed over time. Moderate to severe hot flashes and night sweats • Sleep disruption related to night sweats • Prevention of bone loss in selected patients • Vaginal dryness and irritation • Painful intercourse related to menopausal tissue changes • Certain urinary symptoms associated with genitourinary syndrome of menopause • SMART PATIENT QUESTION Which symptoms are most likely to improve with this particular treatment? 07

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY KNOW YOUR OPTIONS Three Treatment Options. Different Needs. ESTRADIOL TRANSDERMAL PATCHES Systemic Estrogen Therapy Deliver estrogen through the skin to help treat symptoms such as hot flashes and night sweats. ORAL MICRONIZED PROGESTERONE Uterine Protection With Systemic Estrogen Often prescribed alongside systemic estrogen for women with a uterus. VAGINAL ESTRADIOL CREAM Targeted Vaginal Estrogen Therapy Treats menopause-related vaginal dryness, irritation, and painful intercourse through local application. These are not necessarily alternatives to one another. Some women may need more than one treatment. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps offers multiple options; a licensed provider determines the appropriate treatment. SMART PATIENT QUESTION Which treatment addresses my symptoms, and why might I need one medication or a combination? 08

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY ESTRADIOL PATCHES Understanding Estradiol Transdermal Patches Estradiol patches deliver estrogen through the skin into the bloodstream. They are commonly used to treat moderate to severe hot flashes and night sweats associated with menopause. The estradiol patches prescribed through WellPeps are manufactured, FDA-approved products, not compounded preparations. POTENTIAL ADVANTAGES IMPORTANT CONSIDERATIONS THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Your provider determines whether systemic estrogen is appropriate and selects the dose and formulation. No daily oral estrogen tablet • Steady delivery through the skin • Different strengths for individual needs • Observational studies suggest a lower blood-clot risk than oral estrogen, although individual risks still matter • Apply and replace as instructed • Skin irritation or adhesion difficulties may occur • Systemic estrogen has contraindications and potential risks • Women with a uterus generally require appropriate endometrial protection • SMART PATIENT INSIGHT How estrogen is delivered matters; formulations differ in benefits, risks, and practical considerations. 09

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY PROGESTERONE Why Is Progesterone Often Prescribed With Estrogen? For women with a uterus, systemic estrogen without adequate progestogen can increase the risk of endometrial hyperplasia and endometrial cancer. Progesterone helps protect the uterine lining. Oral micronized progesterone may be prescribed alongside systemic estrogen, continuously or cyclically depending on the regimen. Important points: Oral micronized progesterone is made both as an FDA-approved manufactured product and as a compounded preparation. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved. Ask your provider which one you are prescribed. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Your provider considers uterine status, regimen, and medical history. Not every woman taking estrogen needs progesterone Women who have had a hysterectomy often do not require it Dose and schedule depend on the estrogen regimen and medical history Oral progesterone can cause dizziness or drowsiness Progesterone should not be assumed to independently treat every menopause symptom SMART PATIENT QUESTION Do I need progesterone with my estrogen treatment, and what purpose does it serve? 10

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY VAGINAL HEALTH Vaginal Dryness, Discomfort & Menopause Declining estrogen can affect vaginal and urinary tissues, contributing to genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM). Symptoms may include vaginal dryness, irritation, discomfort during intercourse, burning, soreness, urgency, and recurrent urinary tract infections. Unlike hot flashes, these symptoms may persist or worsen without treatment. Low-dose vaginal estradiol cream delivers estrogen locally and is used to treat these symptoms. The vaginal estradiol cream prescribed through WellPeps is a compounded preparation made by a state- licensed pharmacy. Compounded medications are not FDA-approved and have not been evaluated by FDA for safety, effectiveness, or quality. Because systemic absorption is generally low with appropriately prescribed low-dose vaginal estrogen, it may suit some women who do not need systemic therapy. Progesterone generally is not required solely for low-dose local vaginal estrogen, but unexpected vaginal bleeding requires evaluation. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps offers vaginal estradiol options for eligible patients. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT Vaginal health is part of overall health. These symptoms are common, treatable, and worth discussing. 11

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY SAFETY Is Menopausal Hormone Therapy Safe? Benefits and risks depend on age, time since menopause, medical history, formulation, dose, and route. For many healthy women younger than 60 or within about 10 years of menopause onset, systemic therapy may have a favorable benefit-risk balance for bothersome symptoms when no contraindications exist. It may not be appropriate with: A history of breast cancer or other complex conditions may require specialist evaluation. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Eligibility is determined through individualized medical review; not every patient qualifies. Certain estrogen-sensitive cancers Prior blood clots or clotting disorders Stroke or certain cardiovascular conditions Unexplained vaginal bleeding Significant liver disease SMART PATIENT QUESTION What are the benefits and risks given my age, symptoms, and medical history? 12

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY PERSONALIZED TREATMENT The Right Treatment Depends on Your Symptoms Two women of the same age can experience menopause very differently. One may struggle with hot flashes and sleep; another may have vaginal dryness without hot flashes; a third may have symptoms with another medical cause. A provider considers: Most bothersome symptoms Age and menopause stage Whether you have a uterus Medical and family history Medications and risk factors Treatment goals and preferences Response to prior treatments Nonhormonal prescription treatments and lifestyle measures may also be appropriate. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps emphasizes individualized decisions, not the same combination for everyone. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT The best regimen is not necessarily the most extensive; it is the one that fits your needs. 13

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY FOLLOW-UP CARE Hormone Therapy Shouldn’t End With a Prescription Menopause treatment often needs reassessment. Symptoms change, side effects can occur, and a regimen may require adjustment. Appropriate follow-up can include: There is no one treatment duration for everyone. Some patients use therapy briefly; others continue longer following individualized medical discussion. THE WELLPEPS APPROACH WellPeps is designed around provider-guided care and appropriate follow-up. Reviewing symptom improvement Evaluating side effects Discussing unexpected bleeding Updating medical history Assessing dose and formulation Determining whether testing is needed Periodically reviewing benefits and risks SMART PATIENT QUESTION How will treatment be monitored if my symptoms or medical needs change? 14

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY USE THE CHECKLIST The Smart Patient Checklist Before starting menopausal hormone therapy, ask: 01 Understanding Your Health Will my symptoms and menopause stage be evaluated? Will other possible causes be considered? Is laboratory testing useful for my situation? 02 Understanding Your Treatment Do I understand systemic versus vaginal estrogen? If I have a uterus, has progesterone been discussed? Why is this treatment and dose recommended? Have appropriate nonhormonal alternatives been discussed? 03 Understanding Safety Have my personal and family histories been reviewed? Do I understand benefits, risks, and side effects? Is my medication FDA-approved or compounded? 04 Understanding Ongoing Care Will I have appropriate follow-up? What should I do if symptoms persist or bleeding occurs? Do I understand medication, testing, and provider costs? THE WELLPEPS APPROACH Personalized care begins with understanding your health and evaluating appropriate options. SMART PATIENT INSIGHT A quality program helps you understand what you’re taking, why, and how your health will be monitored. 15

SMART PATIENT GUIDE TO WOMEN’S HORMONE THERAPY FINAL THOUGHTS Menopause Changes Things. Understanding Your Options Changes Everything. Perimenopause and menopause are natural stages of life, but the symptoms women experience deserve attention. For some women, hormone therapy provides meaningful relief. For others, nonhormonal treatments or different approaches are more appropriate. Being a Smart Patient means understanding symptoms, knowing options, asking questions, and working with a qualified provider. The goal isn’t to reverse menopause. It’s to make informed decisions about health and quality of life. 18

Report unexpected vaginal bleeding to a healthcare professional.
